title: the pipeline's merge step on a protected repo: ask GitHub to auto-merge on green instead of merging inside the build that is the required check
description:
scripts/ci-merge.sh (the last step of a PR build, .buildkite/pipeline.yml) squash-merges the PR with PUT /repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N/merge. On bead-loop that can never succeed: main's branch protection requires the status check `buildkite/bead-loop`, and that check *is* the build the step runs in, so GitHub answers `405: Required status check "buildkite/bead-loop" is pending` (build #19 on PR #39, 2026-09-20), the step exits 1, and the failure turns the required check red — a green build reported as a failed one. Every bead-loop PR so far was merged by hand for this reason; on inquire-platform the same script works only because that repo is private with no branch protection. `enforce_admins` is on, so there is no bypass. The `automerge` label was created on bead-loop and deleted again the same day: with it, the loop's own PRs here would go red on this step and be sent back as "CI red".

Fix, in scripts/ci-merge.sh: when the PUT answers 405 and the message names a pending required status check, do not fail — enable GitHub's auto-merge on the PR instead (public repos have it), and exit 0 saying so. GraphQL: first `query { repository(owner:, name:) { pullRequest(number:) { id } } }` for the node id, then `mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId:, mergeMethod: SQUASH, expectedHeadOid: SHA}) { pullRequest { autoMergeRequest { enabledAt } } } }` — the same token (an installation token with pull_requests: write may call GraphQL). GitHub then merges the moment this build's status turns green, which is the outcome the label asked for; if auto-merge is already enabled, treat that as done. Any other 405 (conflicts) stays a failure as today. Then, since the label is the opt-in, create the `automerge` label on bead-loop again (`gh label create automerge`) — the loop labels every PR it opens under merge = "pipeline" and holds the bead when it cannot. The merge watcher (src/merge.rs, "pipeline") already closes the bead once the PR is MERGED. README: the Checks and the pipeline section says the step merges; say when it asks GitHub to instead. inquire-platform's scripts/ci-merge.mjs is the same script in node and should get the same branch, in its own PR there.

Proof is a shell test, since the pipeline cannot run here: a fake `curl` on PATH (test/bin has the pattern) that answers the PUT with 405 and that message, then answers the two GraphQL calls; the script exits 0 and its output says auto-merge was enabled with the expected head; a 405 with another message still exits 1.
acceptance_criteria: On a PR build of bead-loop with the automerge label, the :github: automerge step exits 0 and the PR merges once the build's status is green (seen on the first labelled PR after this lands). A test under test/ (a case in run.sh or a new script the gate runs) drives scripts/ci-merge.sh with a stub curl: 405 "Required status check ... is pending" → the GraphQL enablePullRequestAutoMerge call is made with the build's sha and the script exits 0; 405 with any other message → exit 1; 200 → "merged" as today. shellcheck passes; the whole gate in .bead-loop.toml passes.

title: a repeated hold re-arms its backoff: the same reason again touches held/ID, so a bead the server keeps refusing is retried every 5 min, not every pass
description:
On 2026-09-20 between 16:00 and 17:40 UTC the Claude lane ran inq-8gg.8 781 times — one `claude -p` every ~7 s, each answered with "You've hit your session limit", each logged as a hold "no failure charged" (the scoreboard counts them as 800 empty rounds in the week; ~/.local/state/bead-loop/inquire-platform/logs/inq-8gg.8.20260920T16*.worker.jsonl are the empty files, their .err the message).

The cause is in src/state.rs `Repo::hold`: when the reason is the same as the one already in held/ID it returns false *without writing the file*, so the file's mtime — which `round::hold_expired` (src/round.rs) reads through `held_since` as the hold's age — stays at the first hold. Once that is BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF (300 s) old, every later hold with the same reason is expired the moment it is placed; `round::hold` then rings the bell (`repo.wake()`), the lane looks again at once, picks the same bead, runs the harness, gets the same refusal, holds again — a tight loop rung by its own bell. The second hold was meant to be silent (no second note on the bead, no second log line), not free of backoff.

Fix: in `Repo::hold`, when the reason is unchanged, touch the file (crate::util::touch, or rewrite it) before returning false, so the backoff clock restarts from the latest hold. Keep the return value as it is: the caller's note and log line still happen once per reason. The unit test `hold_is_said_once_per_reason` in src/state.rs gains the mtime check; `test/run.sh` `case_harness_down_is_held` (or a new case) proves the wiring: with BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF=2 and the harness stub answering nothing, a `--once tick` right after the second hold does not run the worker again, and one two seconds later does.

Related, not this bead: bl-btp (exponential backoff and park after a day) and bl-ycs (a provider down holds the lane, not each bead) build on this; this one only makes the existing 5 min backoff hold true on the second and every later hold.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test state::tests::hold_is_said_once_per_reason passes with an added assertion that a second `hold` with the same reason leaves `held_since` no older than the moment of that second hold (set the file's mtime back first, e.g. with libc::utimensat as review_queue_is_fewest_failures_then_oldest does, and check it moved forward). test/run.sh has a case where, with BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF=2 and a harness that exits with no output, two ticks in a row make one worker call each (the hold, then the retry after the backoff) and a third tick inside the two seconds makes none — the stub's $TEST_CTRL/calls counts them. The whole gate in .bead-loop.toml passes.

title: Add imkarrer/bead-loop to the Buildkite GitHub App, so Buildkite posts commit statuses and the GitHub Action can go
description: You asked to disable the GitHub Action now that Buildkite builds every push and PR. Main's branch protection requires the status context 'ci' (the Action), and Buildkite is not posting any status on bead-loop commits (checked on 10c4ff8: only github-actions' ci) although the pipeline object has publish_commit_status = true — inquire-platform's does post (buildkite/inquire-platform). The difference is the Buildkite GitHub App's repository access: bead-loop is public and not in the App's selected repositories, so Buildkite can only receive the webhook, not write statuses. Human step: github.com/settings/installations → the Buildkite app → add imkarrer/bead-loop. Then I switch main's required check to buildkite/bead-loop and delete .github/workflows/ci.yml (pipeline settings need no change).
acceptance_criteria: A Buildkite status appears on a bead-loop commit; then the workflow is deleted and the required check swapped in one PR.
close_reason: done: the repo was added to the Buildkite GitHub App; buildkite/bead-loop posts on every commit; main's required check is buildkite/bead-loop and .github/workflows/ci.yml is deleted (claude-lane 48dd840). homelab and agent-hub pipelines have the same gap — add them to the App too if their statuses are wanted on GitHub.

title: Deploy via flox: a tree environment on this box, or a published package pulled by generation?
description: Today deploy is git pull + cargo build --release on this box (bead-loop-deploy.timer, ~2-3 min cold). Two flox shapes, both already in the homelab: (a) TREE — the units run 'flox activate -d ~/src/bead-loop -- bead-supervisor run' off the live checkout, the binary built there by 'flox build' from a [build] table; no catalog, no signing, deploy stays a pull. (b) PACKAGE — CI does 'flox build' + 'flox publish' to the Flox catalog on green (needs a catalog org and a signing key), the box pulls a generation like agent-hub's floxhub kind and never runs cargo. (a) is a day and needs nothing from you; (b) is cleaner and needs: which catalog org, where the signing key lives, and whether the workstation may pull from FloxHub unattended.
acceptance_criteria: An answer choosing (a) or (b); for (b) the org name and where the key goes. The floxify beads then unblock.
close_reason: decided: (b) — a published flox package on the Flox catalog, built and published by CI on green, pulled by generation on the workstation; cargo leaves the box. bl-s89 unblocks; bl-cyx (the [build] table) is its first step.

title: notify: post to the channel of your choice when a bead needs you, Claude signs out, or the loop goes down
description: After the decision on where (see the decision bead). src/notify.rs: notify(kind, text) reads 'notify' from the global config (ntfy://topic or a webhook url), POSTs through curl (the stub in test/bin records it), never blocks a round. Callers: send_back when it parks, hold (once per reason), the merge watcher's holds, claude_ok turning false, recover at start ('the loop is back'). A daily digest of Needs you at 'notify_digest = "09:00"'. The page shows the channel and the last post. README: the Config table and Watching it.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh: parking a bead posts once (the stub curl log has the topic and the text); a hold posts once per reason; a second pass posts nothing; no 'notify' key posts nothing. Documented.
close_reason: not wanted: the human is told in the UI, not by a channel (bl-st2). The page's Needs you with a clear question/reason is bl-s8k.

title: Where should the loop tell you it needs you? (ntfy topic / Discord webhook / nothing)
description: The loop parks and holds beads for you and shows them on the page — but nothing reaches you when you are not looking at it. The homelab bot already posts to a Discord status channel and an ntfy topic. Which of those (or which other channel) should the loop use, and for what: every bead entering Needs you; Claude signing out; the loop going down; a daily digest at a time you name? Answer with the channel and its address (an ntfy topic name, or where the Discord webhook url lives — a sops secret, ~/.config/bead-loop/notify?).
acceptance_criteria: An answer on this bead naming the channel(s), the address, and the events; the notifications bead then unblocks.
close_reason: decided: the page is the channel — no ntfy/Discord. What is missing is not delivery but the question: Needs you must show WHY (the question or reason) for every entry, and decision beads must appear there with their text. That is bl-s8k, now P1.

title: deploy.sh refused by bd's own export: .beads/interactions.jsonl dirty in the live checkout
description: scripts/deploy.sh exits 1 when the live checkout (~/src/bead-loop) has uncommitted tracked changes — and bd, run by the loop on this repo's own beads, keeps rewriting .beads/interactions.jsonl there (an export of its interaction log; the committed file is empty, see 016c4fe). So every deploy after the loop has claimed, noted or released a bead-loop bead is refused: on 2026-09-20 the timer failed at 19:04, 19:06 and 19:08 with '~/src/bead-loop has uncommitted changes; not touching it / M .beads/interactions.jsonl', and PR #38 reached the box only after a hand revert of that file. The guard is right for real edits (a hand change under the live checkout must not be clobbered by a fast-forward) and wrong for bd's export. In scripts/deploy.sh: ignore changes under .beads/ when deciding whether the checkout is dirty (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -- . ':!.beads'), and before the fast-forward set that file aside (git stash push -m deploy -- .beads/interactions.jsonl, or git checkout -- .beads/ after saving the diff to $STATE_DIR/deploy/<stamp>.patch) so --ff-only cannot fail on it; a tracked change outside .beads/ still refuses as today. Alternatively — decide in the bead — stop tracking the export: git rm --cached .beads/interactions.jsonl and add it to .beads/.gitignore, if bd's own docs allow (its .gitignore says the jsonl files are tracked by default). Files: scripts/deploy.sh, README (the deploy paragraph), and a suite case if test/run.sh covers deploy.sh; else a shell check that a checkout with only .beads/interactions.jsonl modified is deployed and one with src/ modified is refused.
acceptance_criteria: With only .beads/interactions.jsonl modified in the live checkout, scripts/deploy.sh fast-forwards, builds and recycles; with src/main.rs modified it refuses as before; the whole gate passes.

title: lanes per model server: acbox worker rounds and acbox reviews stop colliding
description: The Claude lane is the first lane per server. Generalize per docs/design-lanes-per-server.md: one lane per provider named in the stages (devbox, acbox, claude), each taking any queued round — a worker round for a ready bead, a reviewer round for a bead in review — whose model's provider is its own; review rounds before dev rounds, then fewest failures. pause/resume take a provider. status --json lanes keyed by provider (the page's lane panels follow). The dev/review pair remains the shape when no [[stages]] table names more than one provider.
acceptance_criteria: The lane cases in test/run.sh rewritten for 'stub' as a provider; a case shows an acbox review waiting while an acbox worker round runs and a devbox round proceeding meanwhile; the page shows one panel per provider.

title: wire the second-family reviewer and the utility model into the stages, the opencode provider, and the README
description:
Follows homelab-e00 (a non-Qwen reviewer resident on ac-box, trial gpt-oss-120b) and homelab-8r5 (a small utility model there). Nothing in bead-loop discovers models: they are named in three places that all need the new entries once the backends exist on :8100.

1. ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, provider acbox.models: add the reviewer (tool_call true, limit.context 32768, output 8192) and the utility model; point small_model at acbox/<utility> so opencode's titles and summaries stop landing on an 80B slot. The live loop reads the global config, so this is the change that takes effect.
2. ~/.config/bead-loop/config.toml stages: stage 1 reviewer stays acbox/coder or moves to acbox/<reviewer> (decide from the e00 side-by-side notes); stage 2 (worker acbox/coder) reviewer becomes acbox/<reviewer> instead of acbox/instruct -- that is the pair the different-family rule is for. Keep failures counts.
3. agents/bead-reviewer.md: 'model: acbox/coder' is the default the stage table overrides -- update the comment/default if the reviewer moves; if the chosen model takes a reasoning-effort field (gpt-oss does), decide the level for reviews and set it in the provider options.

title: pause LANE stops the lane before its next round, not only at the top of its loop
description: Seen 2026-09-21 01:36-01:48 UTC: bead-supervisor pause gpu, pause cpu, pause claude (all three pause.* flags in the state dir until 02:07); the journal shows only 'claude lane paused; starting nothing until resume'. At 01:48:14 the cpu lane's round (bead-loop bl-cyx round 4) ended and at 01:48:16 the same lane started inquire-platform inq-85h.18 round 10 (stage 2, acbox/coder): a new round on a paused lane. The gpu lane likewise went on. Cause, src/lanes.rs lane(): the pause flag is read once per pass, at the top of the loop; a lane busy when the flag appears finishes its round and walks on to the next repo in the same pass (and a lane that reviews its own worker rounds goes on to the bead's reviewer round in lane_pass) without reading it. The idle claude lane was at the top of its loop, so it saw the flag. Fix: read the flag before every round -- between repos and before the follow-up reviewer round -- and stop the pass there; the top of the loop then logs the paused line once.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh: pause a lane while its round is in flight (a slow stub worker), let the round end, assert the lane starts nothing more -- neither the next repo's bead nor its own bead's reviewer round -- and logs the paused line once; resume, and it goes on. cargo test: a unit test that the pass over the repos stops at the flag. cargo test and test/run.sh green; the README's pause contract says a round in flight finishes and nothing starts after it.

title: a round whose transcript is only the harness's errors is held, not charged
description: Seen 2026-09-21 01:10 UTC (and 23:41 the night before) while the reviewer model on ac-box was being swapped: inquire-platform inq-85h.17's review by acbox/reviewer exited 1 with a transcript of one event, {"type":"error",..."UnknownError"..."Unexpected server error"...ref err_502a8619}; opencode's log for that ref says ProviderModelNotFoundError: Model not found: acbox/reviewer (the server had not been restarted since opencode.json gained the model). The model never saw the diff, yet the bead was charged a failure (4 -> 5) and escalated to claude/sonnet, which cost a Sonnet review. src/round.rs distinguishes 'exited with no output' (held) from 'exited N' (charged) on AgentRun.empty, which is the log file's length; an error-only transcript is not empty. Fix in src/harness.rs: a transcript with no assistant text and no tool or step events, only the harness's own error events, is a round the model never answered -> AgentRun.empty, with the error's message in AgentRun.error; src/round.rs holds it with that message, for the reviewer and the worker (its main round and its gate-fix round). Same shape as bl-ycs (a provider's server down holds the lane), which probes the server before a round; this covers the error the probe cannot see.
acceptance_criteria: test/bin/opencode gains a server-error mode (the production error event, exit 1) for worker and reviewer; test/run.sh has a case for each: no failure charged, held with the error's message, the same stage retried once the hold aged; cargo test has a unit test on the transcript parse and the hold reason; cargo test and test/run.sh green; the README's outcome row and docs/state-machine.md say so.
